text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The trial of the suspected leaders of the Kaunas criminal group Henrikas Daktaras, 39, should start today in Vilnius.

- The new government does not intend to increase state loans by a single litas, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius told parliament when presenting the 1997 draft budget, which includes 5.78 billion litas of revenues and 6.38 billion of expenses. The planned budget deficit was unchanged at 596 million litas.
- The leader of dairy market in nothern Lithuania Rokiskio Suris (Rokiskis Cheese) decided on Monday to issue shares worth 12 million litas to be invested into development of its production.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas will not say anything about his intentions to run for a second term earlier than October next year, he said in an exclusive interview.

- The licences of some commercial banks which do not meet the requirements of the Bank of Lithuania on January 1, 1997 might be banned from operating, central bank president Reinoldijus Sharkinas told the newspaper.
- After the first reading, parliament approved the draft law to cover Lietuvos Energija's 776 million of state debt. The law intends to cover the debt by issuing government T-bills.
- The four biggest parliament factions, including the coalition partners Homeland Union and the Christian Democrats sharply criticised the draft budget project at its first reading.
- Butinges Nafta registered 71.27 million litas share capital.
